Findings: none, at any severity. Round two confirms no new launch, poll, timer or per-seat I/O. Exact-head CI passed and `just pr-freeze 241` reports FINAL.

## Round-two delta

`git range-diff 872fafab~4..872fafab 2d5b1a9c..d3ea172c` confirms the four original changes are equivalent apart from the difficulty-ledger merge. The two additional commits correct PRD delivery states and add the reviewed fixes/tests.

The registration fix copies the route from the already-resolved same-process predecessor in memory; no new registry lookup, process inspection, status GET or persistence round trip is added. The existing descriptor write persists it. The status client remains one shared client with the same 1 s budget, now refuses redirects, and preserves client-build errors instead of falling back to a client without those settings. Non-2xx/malformed status produces one plain decision; the watch still compares the same `not_listening` state, so these changes introduce no retry or notification loop. New server tasks and hit counters are test-only.

## Cost inventory

| Path | Rate and scaling | Launches |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Spawn/revive gate | At most one loopback status GET per eligible Copilot Claude spawn/revive, with a 1 s request/connect timeout under the existing spawn lock. Other harnesses, opt-out, missing model and non-Claude models make no GET. No retry loop. | 0 additional |
| Proxy watch | One initial read, then one shared 30 s tick (0.0333 GET/s), independent of seat/pane count. One bulk SQLite registry list per tick (including the existing schema check), filtered to untombstoned Copilot descriptors. | 0 |
| Seat split and health | Split is in-memory O(live Copilot seats), not per-seat I/O. `/health` clones the cached status/seat vectors; it does not refresh the sidecar or list the registry. SQL work can scale with registry history; constant request count is not constant CPU. | 0 |
| Prime notices | Only on observed state transitions, plus an unhealthy first read when proxied seats exist. Project primes plus designation are sorted/deduplicated; one persisted FYI per distinct untombstoned prime. No unchanged-state repeats and no forced model wake. | 0 |
| Directory | Builds the route map from its existing bulk registry read, now filtered to live rows; no per-holder status GET. | 0 additional |
| Doctor | On demand only: help/status, daemon ping and node formatter, plus recipe shells. The existing status command also performs its one `/usr/bin/dscl` account check (blueprint k-6). Not a daemon timer or per-seat launch. | Manual only |

`CacheProxy` owns one reusable reqwest client. `TickLoop::run_ticks` awaits `tick()` inside the select branch and uses `MissedTickBehavior::Delay`; reads cannot overlap or accumulate spawned tick tasks, including a slow status GET. The 1 s HTTP budget is below the 30 s interval. Shutdown drains an accepted tick. The cache-proxy source adds no process-launch site, so `crates/testkit/tests/spawn_sites.rs` requires no new counter/exemption. Existing spawn command construction gains env assignments, not another process.

The existing sidecar's lazy readiness checks remain its separate cost: at most the blueprint k-3 successful-cache/failed-cache cadence when status is requested. This review does not claim that a loopback status read eliminates that already-designed upstream work.
